proposed.text: Passenger conveyors (walkalators) in airports must follow the same tactile warning geometry as escalators. Which statement correctly describes the tactile requirement at a walkalator entry and exit?

options.text: 600 mm deep warning tactile blocks placed 300 mm before the belt start and end, covering the full clear width
300 mm deep warning tactile blocks placed 600 mm before the belt start and end, covering the full clear width
600 mm deep warning tactile blocks placed 600 mm before the belt start and end, covering only the centerline
900 mm deep warning tactile blocks placed 300 mm before the belt start and end, covering the full clear width

proposed.rationale: Walkalators follow the same 600 mm depth / 300 mm setback / full-width rule as escalators. The article explicitly states that passenger conveyors follow the same 600 mm / 300 mm tactile rule as escalators and ramps. The approach areas must also be level, surfaces slip-resistant, and handrails provided on both sides at accessible heights. Walkalators are essentially 'flat escalators' for tactile and safety logic.
proposed.explanation: Walkalators use the same 600 mm depth / 300 mm setback / full-width tactile rule as escalators per BP 344.
